title: Why the Volunteer Said No to the Camera
script: Host: [curious] We are filming a fundraising video, and one volunteer refuses to appear. Is that a problem?
Guest: No. Participation in service does not create an obligation to become publicity. Ask what information the campaign truly needs.
Host: The organiser says a smiling group photo will attract more donors.
Guest: [carefully] It may, but consent must still be free. If refusing creates pressure, shame, or a threat to someone's role, the permission is not meaningful.
Host: What alternatives can the team use?
Guest: Film supplies being packed, interview a willing coordinator, show verified totals, or use illustrations. The campaign can demonstrate work without identifying every person involved.
Host: Suppose the volunteer initially agrees and changes her mind after recording.

Guest: The team should have explained withdrawal terms beforehand. If publication has not happened, remove her image. If material is already public, respond promptly and explain what can realistically be taken down.
Host: [thoughtful] Does privacy also apply to aid recipients?
Guest: Even more carefully. Their access to help must never depend on sharing a face, name, diagnosis, or personal hardship. Use only necessary details and obtain specific consent.
Host: Some viewers distrust videos without personal stories.
Guest: Then build trust through audited figures, clear processes, and responsible reporting. Emotional exposure is not the only evidence that work is real.
Host: What about children in the background?
Guest: Avoid identifiable images unless lawful, informed guardian permission and appropriate safeguards are in place. A crowded event is not automatic consent.
Host: [reflective] So the volunteer's “no” can improve the whole campaign.
Guest: Exactly. It reminds the team to ask whether visibility serves the mission or simply makes good intentions easier to display.

quiz.question: What project creates the disagreement about appearing on camera?
options: The team is producing a fundraising video for its service work.
A family supposedly needs rent money that same night.
They do not know she is cooking breakfast at a women's shelter.
Every weekend of care leaves him exhausted as their father's memory worsens.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: The team is producing a fundraising video for its service work.

quiz.question: What should organisers identify before asking volunteers to appear?
options: The claim and its personal details have not been verified.
They should decide what information the campaign genuinely requires.
She declines and recommends interviewing the shelter's founder instead.
She felt their father valued Yoga while merely tolerating her.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: They should decide what information the campaign genuinely requires.

quiz.question: When does a volunteer's apparent permission cease to be meaningful?
options: A trusted organisation or authorised coordinator should check it privately.
The kitchen exists because of the founder's sustained work.
Refusal brings pressure, shame, or a threat to the volunteer's role.
She refuses to make present care depend entirely on past affection.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Refusal brings pressure, shame, or a threat to the volunteer's role.

quiz.question: How can the campaign show its work without filming every volunteer?
options: They should not redistribute documents containing private family details.
Public attention could turn sincere service into a performance.
Siti takes two weekdays while Yoga keeps weekends and shares appointments.
It can film supplies, willing staff, verified totals, or illustrations.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: It can film supplies, willing staff, verified totals, or illustrations.

quiz.question: What possibility should consent procedures explain before recording begins?
options: A participant may agree initially and later withdraw permission.
It can report totals, support categories, and payment records.
She will continue volunteering without photographs or announcements.
Discuss the burden honestly and assign specific, workable shifts.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: A participant may agree initially and later withdraw permission.

quiz.question: What should happen if a participant withdraws before publication?
options: They should ask why and listen before choosing another method.
The team should remove that person's image from the material.
They do not know she is cooking breakfast at a women's shelter.
Every weekend of care leaves him exhausted as their father's memory worsens.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: The team should remove that person's image from the material.

quiz.question: Which condition must never be attached to a recipient's access to aid?
options: The voucher may be unusable, while landlord contact could create risk.
She declines and recommends interviewing the shelter's founder instead.
Aid must not depend on revealing identity, diagnosis, or hardship.
She felt their father valued Yoga while merely tolerating her.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Aid must not depend on revealing identity, diagnosis, or hardship.

quiz.question: How should information about aid recipients be selected for publicity?
options: They should have meaningful input whenever circumstances allow.
The kitchen exists because of the founder's sustained work.
She refuses to make present care depend entirely on past affection.
Use only necessary details covered by specific consent.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Use only necessary details covered by specific consent.

quiz.question: What can establish public trust without emotional personal stories?
options: Audited figures, clear procedures, and responsible reporting.
Thanks for aid is not informed consent to publish hardship.
Public attention could turn sincere service into a performance.
Siti takes two weekdays while Yoga keeps weekends and shares appointments.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Audited figures, clear procedures, and responsible reporting.

quiz.question: Why are children in a crowded background not automatically available to film?
options: Use an established emergency process with verification, privacy, and records.
Crowding does not replace guardian permission and appropriate safeguards.
She will continue volunteering without photographs or announcements.
Discuss the burden honestly and assign specific, workable shifts.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Crowding does not replace guardian permission and appropriate safeguards.
